description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §4.2's RIGHT-HAND-SIDE structural `D` rule, in BOTH of its halves. RESOLVE: a `D` with `wrt: "t"` (or no `wrt`) whose `args[0]` is a bare reference to an unknown that CARRIES a differential equation names that unknown's tendency and is substituted during flattening, recursing through chained tendencies — so `dxdt ~ D(x, t)` is `-k*x`, and a model's scoped `D(Chem.A, t)` is the mass-action tendency §7.4 generated for the sibling reaction system. REFUSE: a structural `D` that resolves to NOTHING — one over an observed, over a parameter, or over a compound expression — is a rewrite-target reaching evaluation, and a conforming runtime MUST report `unlowered_operator` rather than invent a value for it, IN PARTICULAR NOT `0`. The two halves are gated together on purpose. Before this category all three Rust evaluators answered `D(anything) = 0` "for parity" with one another, so three shipped documents (`tests/end_to_end/land_atmosphere_hydrology.esm`, `tests/events/financial_climate_scenarios.esm`, `tests/valid/scoped_refs_nested.esm`) computed silent zeros and an inline test asserting a species tendency at t = 0 graded a configuration the model never ran; Python meanwhile refused BOTH halves with `unlowered_operator`, so the bindings disagreed in opposite directions on the same document. The refusal half is the one that can silently rot: `0` is a plausible-looking number, and `d_of_parameter` deliberately asserts `expected: 0.0` so a binding that invents the value is caught by the OUTCOME contract and not by the arithmetic. VERDICTS and outcome CLASSES are compared, not a numeric golden: a refusal has no actual to record, and each binding's diagnostic text differs while the `unlowered_operator` code (esm-spec §9.6.3 constraint 6) is the cross-binding contract.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator / inline test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator / inline test runner
scope_excluded.julia: TWO gaps in `run_pde_tests` — the runner every inline-test category drives — neither of them in the §4.2 transform itself. (1) It cannot READ a 0-D observed: `_evaluate_assertion`'s pointwise branch resolves the asserted name against the STATE VECTOR alone (`_scalar_slot`, src/pde_inline_tests.jl:1227) with no state-free-observed fallback of the kind Rust's `scalar_observed` and Python's `_scalar_observed` provide, so every assertion here answers `scalar state '<name>' not found`. (2) It does not REFUSE an unresolvable right-hand-side `D`: the three refusal fixtures build and solve without complaint and only fail at the assertion lookup, so the `unlowered_operator` contract is unmet on this path (the gate in `tree_walk/compile.jl` belongs to the OTHER runner). Julia DOES implement the resolve half — `flatten` step 3c — and that is pinned separately by `rhs_time_derivative_resolution_test.jl`, which asserts it through a STATE the runner can read (`l(3) = 31` requires the chained tendency to have resolved). A binding GAP, not a design decision: remove this entry once `run_pde_tests` can read a 0-D observed and refuses an unlowered `D`.

cases.note: Anchor: the ODE state itself, so a document that failed to build is distinguishable from one that resolved wrongly.
OWN-STATE form. D(x, t) = -kx*x = -3*2. The pre-fix Rust answer was exactly 0.
The tendency that the chained one names: d(b)/dt = 5 over [0, 3].
CHAINED form: d(l)/dt = sla*d(b)/dt = 10, so l(3) = 1 + 30. A binding that resolves only one level deep, or that zeroes the inner D, leaves l at its default 1.
SCOPED form: D(Chem.A, t) = -k*A = -0.5*4, a tendency that exists only because §7.4 generated it from the reaction list. This is the shape the reporter of issue #206 needed.

combo has no d(combo)/dt equation. Chain-ruling through its definition would be symbolic differentiation, which the format does not define. The mathematically intended -12 must NOT be produced either — the contract is refusal, not a different number.

The sharpest case. A constant's derivative really is 0, and 0 is exactly what the pre-fix bindings returned for EVERY unresolvable D — so the fixture asserts `expected: 0.0` and a binding that answers it PASSES on the number while failing this category. That is the whole point of pinning the outcome class.
args[0] is an operator node, not a bare reference, so there is nothing to look up. Distributing D over the product is symbolic differentiation.
